newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares reverse course and end with gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares reverse course and end with gains.

text.p: German shares recovered from slight weakness during bourse dealings on Monday to later post gains in IBIS activity, traders said.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 15.61 points at 3,232.57 points but posted gains in IBIS dealings to end the day up 11.13 points at 3,260.30.
"After 11 days of record gains, a small break did us some good," said one Frankfurt trader.
He said investors were hoping for a period of consolidation to underpin the recent hefty gains and allow for the market to keep moving higher by making the DAX appear still attractive.
But traders said the dollar's surge toward 1.70 marks in late afternoon dealings prompted a renewed bout of buying despite limited market interest due to a U.S. market holiday.
Carmaker shares were at the centre of attention as Volkswagen AG announced it was curbing output due to parts shortages from Spanish suppliers.
VW shares ended bourse trade down 10.25 points at 806.25 marks but recovered in IBIS to trade at 810 marks.
Daimler-Benz AG, which makes Mercedes vehicles, was also under pressure, falling 2.80 marks to 122.15 marks after suspending output of its Vito vans at a Spanish factory.
Among other shares, airline Lufthansa fell 2.53 percent to 23.10 marks after announcing plans to reduce fares on some German routes due competition from rival airline Deutsche BA.
Insurer Allianz was higher, rising 10 marks to 3,268 marks to a new record high at 3,310 marks ahead of its results news conference on Wednesday.
